title: Les temps sur une ligne
subtitle: The French tenses on one timeline
review: Made by Claude from the old tenses overview and its timeline picture. The futur simple examples and the English glosses of the verb forms are new: check them.
intro: Move along the line from the past to the future. Each point is a tense: see when it is used, how it is built, and what one verb looks like in it. Two points sit off the line: they say how you see an action, not when it happens.
img_alt: An illustrated river of time: imparfait and passé composé in the past, the présent as the anchor, futur proche and futur simple ahead, with the conditionnel and the subjonctif below as tenses of perspective

tenses.name: plus-que-parfait
tenses.hint: The past of the past: it was already over before another past moment.
tenses.use: An action completed before another past action.

examples.en: I had forgotten my wallet.

examples.fr: Elle **était déjà partie** quand je suis arrivé.
examples.en: She had already left when I arrived.
We had never seen that.
He had told me he would come.

tenses.name: imparfait
tenses.hint: Ongoing, habitual, descriptive: a stretch of the past, not a point.
tenses.use: The background of a story, what was going on, and what used to happen.

examples.en: I didn't know.
That's what I was looking for.

examples.fr: Quand on **était** jeunes, on **jouait** souvent au badminton.
examples.en: When we were young, we used to play badminton often.

tenses.name: passé composé
tenses.hint: A completed point in the past.
tenses.use: Past actions and completed events. In speech it replaces the passé simple.

examples.en: I made a mistake.
It's done, it's over.
I have never been to France.

tenses.name: présent
tenses.hint: Now: the anchor every other tense is measured from.
tenses.use: Current actions, habits, general truths, and the near future.
tenses.structure: subject + verb with the present endings

examples.en: It happens to me sometimes.
I drink lots of water in the morning.
Giraffes have a long neck.
He's coming tomorrow.

tenses.name: futur proche
tenses.hint: The cause is already present: it is planned, or about to happen.

examples.en: I'm going to bed.

examples.fr: Je sais pas si ça **va marcher**.
examples.en: I don't know if it's going to work.
He's going to be happy.

tenses.name: conditionnel présent
tenses.hint: A future seen from a condition: it floats above the line because it may never happen.
tenses.structure: infinitif (or the irregular futur stem) + the imparfait endings

examples.en: I'd like a tea.
Would you like to see it?
How would I know?
What would you do in my place?

tenses.name: futur simple
tenses.hint: The standard future: predictions, promises, plans further away.
tenses.use: Future actions, predictions and promises. More formal and more distant than the futur proche.

examples.en: I'll call you tomorrow.
The weather will be nice this weekend.
We'll see.

tenses.name: subjonctif
tenses.hint: It's not “when”, it's how I see it: a wish, a doubt, a need, a feeling.
tenses.use: After expressions of feeling, wish, doubt or necessity, when the two clauses have different subjects.
tenses.structure: main clause (indicatif) + **que** + subject + verb in the subjonctif

examples.fr: Je suis content que tu **ailles** mieux.
examples.en: I'm glad that you're feeling better.
I want you to come early.
I can't wait for you to see it.

examples.fr: Il faut que je **fasse** une pause.
examples.en: I have to take a break.
Do you want me to do it?
